blocking.where: RESULT.md 'Answer', 'Where the gaps arise' (lines 26-29); section 5 table row 'Mac publish interval at least half the backend gap'; section 4 'The fatal gap' (lines 173-177); 'Which stall ended which run', row diag_v31_clock04 (line 221); 'What v32 can and cannot change', B and 'For Dr Sun' (lines 254-261). PLAN.md 'Decision and basis' ('all 20 backend gaps over 150 ms arose in the Mac-side Newton worker, before publishing (measured)'; 'diag_v31_clock04 ended on B') and 'Not addressed by v32' ('They can still stretch a step past 0.25 s, and they ended diag_v31_clock04'). REVIEW_RESPONSE_round1.md B2 ('All 20 arose before publishing').
blocking.finding: The new localisation is wrong for 13 of the 20 gaps, and it is labelled 'measured'. In every B gap the worker kept publishing inside the window: 3-6 intermediate poses, with the longest interval between consecutive Mac publishes 38.9-87.1 ms, which is 25-55% of the backend gap. In clock04's fatal 297.3 ms gap, poses were published at 0, 83.5, 121.6, 146.9, 179.7, 216.6, 244.5 and 278.6 ms, so the longest interval was 83.5 ms. Those poses reached the bridge and were superseded there. So the part of each B gap beyond about 40-87 ms arose after publishing, at a location the record itself calls unmeasured. With lossless delivery none of the 13 B gaps would have exceeded about 90 ms, and clock04 would not have tripped the 0.25 s gate; no step in that window exceeded 177 ms. The test used for 'arose before publishing' (the two received poses were published at least half the backend gap apart) holds by construction whenever both received poses have small receipt delays. It therefore cannot locate a gap made of superseded poses. Only the 7 A gaps, with consecutive poses, arose before publishing. Consequences: (1) 'Every one of them arose on the Mac, before publishing (measured)' contradicts the record's own B bullet ('poses published during the slow window never reached the backend'). (2) The clock04 source row, 'B, measured', leaves out the post-publish part that made the gap fatal. (3) PLAN's 'can still stretch a step past 0.25 s, and they ended diag_v31_clock04' is not what happened. (4) 'Removing B's effect needs a change to what the gate measures' is not supported for the diagnostic runs' B gaps. A delivery-side change would have kept those gaps under 90 ms: in the worker's sender, the host-VM path, or the bridge's newest-only 10 ms timer, once L1 has located the delay. The gate time-base option is needed only for producer-side stalls such as v31's 288 ms step with no publish.
blocking.evidence: Scratch recomputation using the endpoints in pose_gaps_*.json and publish times from diagnostics/substeps.npy (every fifth substep). Longest intervals between consecutive publishes in the B gaps: clock03 69.7, 38.9, 79.8, 83.5, 67.8, 82.2 and 69.4 ms; clock04 87.1, 62.8, 60.8, 73.8, 83.9 and 83.5 ms. In the A gaps the longest interval is the whole gap, 161-274 ms. Every frame the worker sent was accepted at the bridge: clock04 sent 79,538 frames = 75,751 accepted states + 3,787 clouds; clock03 sent 118,864 = 113,204 + 5,660.
blocking.required_fix: State that A gaps arose before publishing (no pose was published). State that B gaps combine a worker slowdown (publishes 20-87 ms apart instead of about 10 ms) with the post-publish superseding of 3-6 poses, that both are needed to exceed 150 ms, and that the superseding's location is unmeasured. In section 5, replace the non-discriminating row with 'longest interval between consecutive Mac publishes' (A 161-274 ms, B 39-87 ms). Rewrite the clock04 source row, PLAN.md's basis and its 'Not addressed' text, and RESULT's 'What v32 can and cannot change' and 'For Dr Sun', so the delivery-side option (after L1 locates the delay) sits next to the gate time-base option.

blocking.where: versions/v32/PLAN.md 'Stall classes' and L1 criteria 2-3; PHYSICAL_RUN_PLAN.md 'Expected signals'; audits/2026-09-29_wall_clock_chain/diag_worker.py step() (lines 61-82); RESULT.md 'Answer', A bullet ('Four signs occur together (measured)'), and the section 5 rows 'Process runnable wait in the window' and 'Efficiency-core share'; analyze_pose_gaps.py lines 72-95.
blocking.finding: The stall classes cannot be evaluated between steps. 'Process-wide hold' needs the physics thread's off-CPU time and the process runnable wait, and 'scheduling-type' needs the runnable wait. But diag_worker records rusage and thread CPU only as deltas taken inside Lite3Newton.step, so nothing covers the time between steps. Any gap between steps over 100 ms is therefore 'unclassified' and fails criterion 3 whatever its cause. That contradicts 'scheduling-type stalls ... do not fail L1', and criterion 2 cannot detect a hold between steps under its own definition. The same limit affects the record. Five A gaps were between-step freezes: clock03's 159, 200, 211 and 262 ms and clock04's 181 ms. For them, the signs 'runnable wait about 0' and 'efficiency-core share at most 0.12', labelled measured, come from the in-step deltas of the steps overlapping the window, not from the freeze. analyze_pose_gaps sums whole overlapping steps. The same summing gives one B gap a 724 ms runnable wait, mostly from a 188.8 ms step that lies largely before the window. The A reading of those five still rests on measured signs: the clock client stopped, the external probe woke on time, and in clock04 the logged 176 ms collection. But two of the 'four measured signs' were not measured for them.
blocking.evidence: diag_worker.py stores only the deltas (after - usage, thread_after - thread_cpu) in each steps.npy row and no absolute values. The pose_gaps entries for between-step A gaps show runnable waits of -1.3 to 1.5 ms, taken from the adjacent steps.
blocking.required_fix: Before L1, record absolute rusage_v6 values and main-thread CPU at each step's start and end, or add explicit between-step rows, so that between-step deltas exist. Then state the between-step rule, for example: a hold is main-thread CPU and process runnable wait both under 20 ms between the steps, plus a clock-client pause over 100 ms (a collection on the main thread is caught by criterion 1). Alternatively, define the between-step classes only from signals that are recorded: an overlapping collection, a clock-client pause, watchdog lateness and the external probe. In RESULT.md, limit the 'measured' runnable-wait and efficiency-core signs to the in-step A gaps, and mark them as not measured in the window for the between-step ones.

non_blocking.where: PLAN.md 'The collection first' ('traverses only objects created since the previous freeze') and 'Remaining costs, measured by K3'
non_blocking.finding: The first explicit collection, before the loop, covers the whole start-up heap. It took 82.1 ms in K3 (the first explicit event in collect_freeze/gc_events.npy), which is outside K3(a) and L1 criterion 1 by design. In the live run it comes right after commands.start() and telemetry.start(), while the clock client (200 ms TTL) and command receiver are running. No pose flows yet, and the backend's odom check runs only once there is an owner, so the risk is low.
non_blocking.suggestion: State this cost in PLAN.md and report its duration in L1.

non_blocking.where: PLAN.md 'The freeze' ('middle collections run at most about once per window')
non_blocking.finding: Under v32's schedule, K3 logged 95 middle and 1,155 young collections in 946 steps, against 16 and 174 without freezing. The likely cause is that each explicit full collection clears the free lists, and refilling them inflates the young-generation count. Each collection is cheap: young at most 0.10 ms, middle at most 0.35 ms.
non_blocking.suggestion: Correct the sentence; it is true only for the freeze-only schedule.

non_blocking.finding: 'Garbage collectable after unfreeze' is an upper bound. It also counts unfrozen garbage still pending since the last window (steps 901-946); the 'none' mode alone shows 18,019 such objects. So 'Garbage frozen for good: 1,772' overstates. Also, the live loop reads backend_latest.json, which releases the GIL, between the scan submission and the window's collection. The scanner can then be mid-construction at the freeze more often than in the replay. The worst case is about one kernel graph (about 0.14 MB) per window, about 80 MB over a 600 s run.
non_blocking.suggestion: Isolate the leak with gc.collect() before gc.unfreeze(), relabel the number as an upper bound, and check peak RSS in L1 and L2.

non_blocking.finding: diag_worker's gc_events has no flag marking explicit collections (K3's bench has one), so 'no automatic full collection' needs a rule to tell explicit from automatic generation-2 collections.
non_blocking.suggestion: Pre-register the rule, for example: a main-thread generation-2 collection starting between steps right after a step whose state_sequence is divisible by 50 is explicit. Or wrap gc.collect in diag_worker to mark them (observation only).

non_blocking.where: PLAN.md exposure rule ('7,100 control steps or 300 s of loop wall time')
non_blocking.finding: Full collections are driven by allocations; in clock04 they came at about 470, 3,660 and 7,090 steps. With 'or', a slow run could reach 300 s with only about 3,000 steps, in which v31 would have had one full collection.

non_blocking.where: container_site/sitecustomize.py (writers at lines 41, 78, 84 and 98; flush_once at lines 46-53; atexit at line 69)
non_blocking.finding: The writers extend buffers[k] without holding the lock, while flush_once swaps the array and writes the old one. A row appended after the old array was written is lost. The atexit flush can also interleave with the flush thread and write chunks out of time order, and analyze_linux takes np.diff of the publish starts. Lost or out-of-order rows can look like 'not received' or like a callback pause.
non_blocking.suggestion: Take the lock in the writers, or flush by index without swapping, and sort by time in analyze_linux.

non_blocking.finding: The bridge's 'receive' time (receive_monotonic_ns in timed_offer) is taken in its telemetry thread after recv and decode. A late receive therefore cannot separate the host-VM path from starvation of that thread, except through the recorded publish-callback durations and collections. No analysis script yet reads the worker's telemetry_frames_*.npy.
non_blocking.suggestion: Pre-register how the three segments (worker sender, network, bridge) will be split.

non_blocking.finding: The smoke check in the pinned image (Python 3.10.12, three patches loaded) is not in the repository. The docstring names diagnostics/telemetry_frames.npy, but the code writes telemetry_frames_enqueued.npy and telemetry_frames_sent.npy.
non_blocking.suggestion: Store the smoke check's command and output with the audit, and fix the docstring.
